titleZh: 包装少一点，思考多一点

cet4.title: Thinking Beyond the Shopping Bag
cet4.summary: 包装的环境价值不能仅凭纸或塑料的外观判断。首先应理解包装承担的保护、信息与安全功能。

paragraphs.text: A shopper chooses a product with a paper wrapper and feels that the decision is simple. Paper looks familiar, while plastic is often linked with waste. Yet the environmental value of packaging cannot always be judged by appearance alone. A useful question is what the package needs to do. It may protect food, prevent damage or provide information that helps someone use a product safely.
paragraphs.translation: 包装的环境价值不能仅凭纸或塑料的外观判断。首先应理解包装承担的保护、信息与安全功能。

paragraphs.text: Using less material is helpful when the product still reaches the buyer in good condition. However, removing protection can sometimes lead to more waste if the contents are damaged. A reusable container also needs to be used repeatedly to serve its purpose. Buying several new containers and leaving them in a cupboard does not create the same result as using one container for a long time.
paragraphs.translation: 减量应以产品仍得到适当保护为前提。可重复使用的容器也必须真正反复使用，长期闲置并不会实现同样的价值。

paragraphs.text: What happens after use matters too. A label may say that a material can be recycled, but the local collection service may not accept it. Different materials joined together can be difficult to separate. Clear instructions help only when people have a practical way to follow them. Designers, shops and waste services all influence the choices available to a household.
paragraphs.translation: 材料可回收，不代表当地会收集处理。复合材料难分离，居民需要现实可行的处理方式，设计者、商店与回收服务都影响选择。

paragraphs.text: Consumers can start with a few ordinary questions. Is this much packaging necessary? Can I use the container again? Does my local service collect this material? There may not be a perfect answer for every purchase. Still, paying attention to the whole process is more useful than judging one material by its name. Better packaging is part of a system that includes protection, repeated use and a realistic plan for what comes next.
paragraphs.translation: 消费者可以询问必要性、再次使用及当地收集条件。没有适合所有情况的完美答案，完整过程比单纯材料名称更值得关注。

paragraphs.text: Keeping a container near the place where it will be needed is one way to make reuse easier. A lunch box forgotten at home cannot help with today’s meal. Simple arrangements often decide whether a good intention becomes a repeated habit. The practical details of use deserve as much attention as the promise printed on a package.
paragraphs.translation: 把容器放在需要使用的地方、方便清洁与携带，有助于让重复使用成为习惯。实际使用细节与包装承诺同样值得重视。

questions.prompt: What does the author suggest about judging packaging?
options: Ignore what happens after the purchase.
Consider its function and its whole use process.
Decide only by how natural the material looks.
Assume that all reusable objects have equal effects.
questions.explanation: 文章强调功能、使用和处理的完整过程。

questions.prompt: Why can removing packaging sometimes be unhelpful?
options: The contents may become damaged and wasted.
It always makes products last forever.
It guarantees that no resources are needed.
It prevents every form of transport.
questions.explanation: 如果失去必要保护导致产品损坏，整体浪费可能增加。

questions.prompt: What determines whether a reusable container serves its purpose?
options: Whether it remains new in a cupboard.
Whether it has the longest possible label.
Whether several copies are bought at once.
Whether it is actually used repeatedly.
questions.explanation: 可重复使用的价值依赖实际的重复使用。

questions.prompt: Why is a recyclable label not enough?
options: Households can control every stage of manufacturing.
The label replaces all practical disposal arrangements.
Local services may not collect or process the material.
Every material is collected in exactly the same way.
questions.explanation: 本地收集与处理能力影响最终结果。

questions.prompt: Which attitude best matches the passage?
options: Treat advertising language as complete evidence.
Make informed choices while recognising trade-offs.
Search for one material that is perfect in every situation.
Stop considering the purpose of packaging.
questions.explanation: 作者主张考虑现实条件，而非追求普遍完美的单一材料。

cet6.title: Sustainable Packaging Is a Question of Systems
cet6.summary: 包装的环境价值不能仅凭纸或塑料的外观判断。首先应理解包装承担的保护、信息与安全功能。

paragraphs.text: Environmental claims about packaging often invite a quick judgment based on material: paper appears responsible, plastic appears problematic, and reusable appears preferable to disposable. Such categories can be useful starting points, but they do not provide a complete evaluation. Packaging performs functions, including protecting contents, extending usability and communicating instructions. Any assessment should consider whether those functions are necessary and how they are achieved across the product's journey.
paragraphs.translation: 纸、塑料、可重复使用等分类只是判断起点。包装也承担保护内容、延长可用期与传递说明等功能，需要从完整使用过程评价。

paragraphs.text: Reducing the quantity of material can be beneficial, yet the outcome depends on what follows. A package that uses fewer resources but allows its contents to be damaged may shift waste rather than prevent it. Similarly, the promise of a reusable container depends on repeated use in practice. Production, transport and cleaning all belong in the wider picture. Without making unsupported claims about which option is universally best, consumers can recognise that behaviour and context influence the result as much as the label attached to an object.
paragraphs.translation: 减量若造成产品损坏，可能只是转移浪费。重复使用的价值也取决于真实行为，生产、运输和清洗都需考虑，不能宣称某种选择普遍最好。

paragraphs.text: The end of use introduces another layer of complexity. Technical recyclability does not guarantee that a material will be collected, sorted and processed where the consumer lives. A design combining several materials may make separation difficult, while an unfamiliar disposal instruction may create confusion. Responsibility is consequently distributed across manufacturers, retailers, collection services and households. Asking consumers to make better choices is insufficient if the surrounding system does not offer a realistic route for those choices to succeed.
paragraphs.translation: 技术上可回收不等于当地能完成收集、分类和加工。责任分布在制造、零售、回收与家庭之间，需要支持选择实现的系统。

paragraphs.text: Clear communication should acknowledge these conditions. A useful label explains what action to take and, where necessary, directs users to local guidance. Broad environmental language without an accessible explanation can make comparison harder rather than easier. Businesses can improve the situation by simplifying designs, making reuse convenient and describing the limits of their claims. The aim is not to overwhelm a shopper with technical detail, but to make relevant differences understandable.
paragraphs.translation: 标签应说明可采取的行动，必要时引导到本地指南。简化设计、方便重复使用、解释主张的限制，有助于消费者理解真正相关的差异。

paragraphs.text: For individuals, a practical approach begins with necessity and likely use: how much protection is required, whether an existing container can serve the same purpose, and what collection options are actually available. These questions do not eliminate every trade-off. They encourage attention to a complete sequence rather than a single attractive feature. Sustainable packaging should be evaluated as part of an operating system of production, consumption and recovery, not merely as a material that looks reassuring at the moment of purchase. Comparing these stages can also make a conversation about everyday choices more concrete.
paragraphs.translation: 个人可从保护需求、现有容器和实际回收条件出发。可持续包装应作为生产、消费与回收系统的一部分评价，而非只看购买时令人安心的特征。

paragraphs.text: Convenience helps determine whether intentions become repeated behaviour. A container that is easy to clean, store and carry is more likely to return to use than one that creates a new difficulty each day. Retail arrangements can reinforce this pattern or work against it. Considering these ordinary details shifts the discussion away from an idealised consumer and towards the conditions in which real choices are made. Environmental design needs to work within those conditions.
paragraphs.translation: 清洁、储存和携带的便利性决定了意愿是否转为行动。关注这些细节，能从理想化消费者转向真实决策条件，让环境设计融入日常生活。
